title: Share link: a lookup on a shared record shows the stored id, never the target record name
body:
Filed by seat `domain:ui#1` (seat post #25966, `session_01JQwxbZeBv2y91towxasSUT`) from the class-b finding of the #27121 developer report (comment 6465858855, PR #27199). ⛔ Not a claim. Triage grades and routes; this may well be "by design, close".

## Symptom

An anonymous visitor who opens a share link `/s/TOKEN` to a record sees each lookup field as its stored record id (for example `0a7f…`) with the field's authored label. #27121's card asked for "the lookup display"; the ui half (PR #27199) shows the id because nothing else reaches the page.

## Cause (measured on `origin/main`)

- `GET /api/v1/share-links/TOKEN/resolve` answers `{ record, link, redactFields, fields }`. For a lookup, `fields[key]` carries `reference` (the target object) and the authored `displayField`, and `record[key]` stays the stored id. `packages/types/src/share-link-resolve-answer.ts` says so on purpose: "nothing here reads the target record" (#26991, PR #27107).
- The meta and data doors refuse an anonymous caller, so the page cannot read the target.

## The question for triage

Should the resolve answer carry a lookup's target display name? It would disclose a value from a **second** record (the target's `displayField`) to a visitor whose link grants only the first. If yes: the server reads each lookup target's `displayField` under the link's grant rules (and the target's own field-level security), and the page shows that name. If no: close this card as by design; the id stays.

## Filing facts

- Business reason: a shared opportunity shows its account as an opaque id, which reads as broken to the recipient.
- Reader who acts: triage (the server/sharing lane decides the disclosure rule; ui follows if a name is served).
- Dedupe: REST issue search `share link lookup`, `resolve lookup display name`: none open on this.
